seo_description: Voice-controlled rhythm game using real-time ML audio classification. Beatbox sounds trigger gameplay actions with under 60ms latency.
hero.title: Transientica
hero.subtitle: AudioLab
hero.desc: Beatbox into your mic, play a rhythm game. Real-time ML recognition with under 60ms latency.
features.title: How It Works
features.realtime.title: Low Latency
features.realtime.desc: Under 60ms. That's the ceiling for a rhythm game to feel playable. Small FFT buffers (512 samples), a lean ML pipeline, and UDP for OSC keep it there.
features.ml.title: Learns Your Voice
features.ml.desc: Everyone beatboxes differently. The system trains on your voice and your microphone specifically, so accuracy stays high. Give it 30 examples per sound class, then play.
features.architecture.title: Split Pipeline
features.architecture.desc: Python handles audio analysis and ML inference. Unity handles gameplay. They talk over UDP/OSC, so each side can be debugged and updated on its own.
technical.title: Technical Deep Dive
technical.spectral.title: Spectral Analysis
technical.spectral.desc: Kicks live in the low end. Snares are mostly noise. The classifier picks up on those differences. Spectral centroid, zero-crossing rate, and envelope shape do the heavy lifting to separate the three classes.
technical.optimization.title: Optimization
technical.optimization.desc: 512-sample FFT window (11ms), circular buffer to kill I/O blocking, lightweight SVM (2ms inference vs 15ms for a neural net), UDP transport. Every millisecond counted.
challenges.title: Challenges & Solutions
challenges.c1_problem: First version had 180ms lag. Completely unplayable for a rhythm game.
challenges.c1_solution: Shrunk the FFT window, added a circular buffer, swapped to a lightweight SVM, switched to UDP for OSC. 45ms at 92% accuracy. Done.
challenges.c2_problem: Both have sharp transients and broadband noise. The classifier couldn't tell them apart reliably.
challenges.c2_solution: Added spectral centroid, zero-crossing rate, and envelope shape as features. Built separate models for solo hits vs patterns. That pushed accuracy from 78% to 92%.
challenges.c3_problem: Heavy ML processing caused buffer underruns on slower machines. Audio would just cut out.
challenges.c3_solution: Separated threads with a lock-free ringbuffer. Audio never blocks. ML runs on its own worker thread.
